newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila expects $2.55 bln in pledges at Tokyo meet.
newsitem.headline: Manila expects $2.55 bln in pledges at Tokyo meet.

text.p: The Philippines hopes to get pledges of $2.55 billion in financial assistance during the consultative group meeting with its donors and creditors to be held in Tokyo from December 10 to 11, Finance Secretary Roberto De Ocampo said on Tuesday.
"The country looks forward to additional indications of assistance in this year's meeting, specifically for projects in the social sector," De Ocampo said in a statement.
This will be the sixth consultative group meeting since the Philippine Assistance Programme (PAP) was launched in 1989 to help restructure the Philippine economy.

The meeting will be chaired by the World Bank and will be participated by multilateral institutions such as the International Monetary Fund, the Asian Development Bank, the United Nations Development Programme, and representatives from 22 donor countries and aid agencies.
During the meetings in the last two years, the Philippines generated some $8.6 billion in pledges from donors.

De Ocampo added the meeting will also provide a good opportunity for the Philippine government to present and discuss with the international donor community its structural reform programmes as well as priority projects which may require official development assistance.
